question.summary: Graph-indexed complete invariant families and a free stable invariant algebra are known. A finite-dimensional minimal set for arbitrary mixed two-particle states and the full N-representability constraints remain unknown.
question.importance: Local invariants provide basis-independent coordinates for two-particle states. Expressing N-representability in those coordinates would connect orbit classification to the quantum marginal problem.
question.unresolved: Find a finite-dimensional minimal complete invariant set for mixed symmetric or antisymmetric two-particle states and express N-representability in those invariants.

sourceRefs.statedTitle: Minimal complete set of local invariants for an antisymmetric (or symmetric) 2-particle density matrix

claims.title: The stable invariant algebra has graph-indexed generators
claims.text: Vrana constructs systematic complete families and a free stable algebra, without solving the finite-dimensional minimal mixed-state problem.

claims.title: General two-body N-representability is QMA-complete
claims.text: The complexity theorem gives a strong obstruction to any efficient general criterion, but does not identify the requested minimal invariants.
